jobs.title: The walk
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, hair longer, brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands always in its pockets; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The dog wants out. The strip discovers the beach. Panel 1: a scruffy dog standing at a bedroom door holding a sock in its mouth, looking at a young man at a drawing table (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). Wood says "I'm working.". Panel 2: a standoff between a dog holding a sock at a door and a young man at a drawing table with his pen hovering (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a wide beach in sideways rain, a low-slung dog barking at a breaking wave, a young man behind with his coat pulled over his head, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a young man stopped on a beach looking at light breaking through a spruce grove while a small dog tugs him forward by a sock, no words (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
